supporting_observations.claim: At 13:41:50 UTC, ivy.chen's interactive session opened C:\Users\ivy.chen\Downloads\Statement.docm in Word.
Word spawned PowerShell about two seconds later with -nop, -w hidden, and -enc arguments; the encoded command requests a script from raw.githubusercontent.com.
The proxy recorded a successful GET for https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nwd-it/tools/main/u.ps1, corroborating the script request from the PowerShell command.
PowerShell then spawned rundll32.exe with C:\Users\ivy.chen\AppData\Roaming\svchelper.dll,Init as its command line.

The sequence of a document-launched hidden, encoded PowerShell download followed by a rundll32 invocation of a DLL in the user's Roaming directory strongly supports malicious activity associated with the alert.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied process and network records establish the command line and proxy request, but do not provide the downloaded script's contents or a file hash for it (T043-00128, T043-00132).
The supplied records show a rundll32 invocation referencing svchelper.dll, but do not establish the DLL's contents, signature, or whether it was successfully loaded (T043-00139, T043-00140).
claims_not_established: The available evidence does not establish who authored or delivered Statement.docm, or whether the user knowingly opened it (T043-00124, T043-00125).
The downloaded script's behavior, the DLL's payload, and any resulting impact are not established by the supplied records (T043-00132, T043-00139, T043-00140).
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire Statement.docm and determine its provenance, hash, and macro contents.
Retrieve the exact u.ps1 content served at the recorded time and assess its behavior.
Collect svchelper.dll and determine its hash, signature, provenance, and whether it was loaded.
Review endpoint protection and subsequent host activity for detection, persistence, credential access, or other impact.
unrelated_findings: Separate review: sam.okafor Kerberos activity is recorded from WS-ICHEN-01, followed by a successful network logon to WS-SOKAFOR-01 identifying WS-ICHEN-01 as the workstation. This is worth checking against the stated remote-administration practice, but is not needed to determine the alerted PowerShell activity (T043-00080, T043-00082, T043-00084).
